title: Introduce presubmit-prober-lite and Oxide dep cleanser to reduce CI setup noise
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: The presubmit pipeline has grown noisy and slow due to full toolchain fetches, overly conservative devdep pinning, and repeated cold-start overheads in ephemeral CI runners. Motivation: Reduce pretest latency and flakiness by introducing a lightweight presubmit prober that warms an ephemeral 'shadow' artifact cache, a sparse-fetch wrapper to avoid pulling full toolchains for quick presubmit lanes, and a small dependency-cleanser (Oxide) that flags / optionally prunes devdeps causing large install graphs. This PR bundles a tooling + workflow refactor to give teams an opt-in fast lane for quick feedback and a hygiene tool to keep CI images and lockfiles lean. Summary of changes: - tools/presubmit-prober/: new Go binary (small, dependency-free) that probes common package registries, exercises cache layers, and warms a shadow cache on the runner prior to heavy installs. It exits 0 on successful warm, non-zero on registries unavailable (used to gate slow lanes). - tools/oxide-dep-cleanser/: Python script + policy rules that detect devdeps larger than XMB or with >N transitive deps; emits a suggested devdep rollback or a Linear ticket. Has a --dry-run mode used in CI. - .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: adds a 'quick-lint' lane that runs the prober + sparse-fetch + lint/test smoke subset for changed packages. Quick lane is opt-in via PR label "quick-feedback" and automatically triggers when change size < 200 LOC and files_changed_count < 10. - ci/ci-setup/sparse-fetch.sh: new wrapper around package managers (npm/pip/go) that uses registry list hints and fetches only declared direct deps for quick lanes. - Docker/ci: small tweaks to the CI image entrypoint to expose shadow-cache dir and make cache permissions deterministic. - docs/dev/ci-guides.md: documents opt-in criteria, observability signals, how to interpret Oxide reports, and rollout plan. Design notes: - The shadow cache is kept in the runner's ephemeral workspace and does not change upstream artifacts; it's purely advisory to reduce network and cold cache penalty. - Oxide deliberately does not edit lockfiles in CI by default; we run it with --dry-run and surface structured findings in presubmit comments. Teams can flip a repo-level config to allow automated patch PRs after manual review. - Quick-lint lane preserves strict unit/integration lanes for main pipeline; fast lane is additive and gated so it cannot replace full checks. Testing done: - Local unit tests for presubmit-prober (registry mocking), oxide (policy fuzzing) - End-to-end smoke on a canary repo with 30 sample PRs: median presubmit setup time reduced from ~125s to ~62s on quick lanes. - Integration: ran full main pipeline twice with the new hooks to ensure no regressions; a flakey integration test surfaced (test/db/timeout) which was unrelated and filed as SUP-2123. Rollout plan: - Start as opt-in for 20% of repos via repo-config opt-in label and selective enabling in .github. - Monitor presubmit latency, flake rate, and Oxide false-positive rate for 2 weeks. - Follow-up: enable auto PR creation for low-risk devdeps after product review. Checklist: - [x] Add presubmit-prober binary and tests - [x] Add Oxide script + policy rules - [x] Wire quick-lint lane and sparse-fetch wrapper - [x] Add docs and observability hooks - [x] Add reviewer feedback fixes (timeouts/logging/metrics) Related work: builds on ENG-4020 (ci sparse-fetch research) and pairs with ENG-4231 (presubmit cost telemetry).
commits_summary: Initial add of presubmit-prober and oxide tools; add sparse-fetch wrapper; update presubmit workflow with quick-lint lane; docs and CI-image tweaks; follow-up commit reduces prober logging and shortens timeouts per reviewer feedback; final commit bumps presubmit workflow to gate by label and change-size heuristics.
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice approach. Please reduce prober log noise and add a single prom metric for warm_duration_ms.
Ava Chen: Addressed — reduced log level and added warm_duration_ms histogram (promclient). PTAL.
Sofia Martinez: Oxide looks useful but I'm worried about false positives on monorepos. Can we add a repo whitelist and a dry-run default?
Ava Chen: Added repo-level opt-in in policies.yaml and made dry-run the default in CI. Also surfaced findings to presubmit comments rather than auto-fixing.
Ravi Iyer: Quick-lint gating looks sane; please ensure the heuristic doesn't run for release/* branches.
Ava Chen: Added explicit branch guard and unit test showing the guard behaviour.
SRE (automated): integration tests had 1 transient DB timeout during runs; reran and passed. Logged SUP-2123 for follow-up.
release_notes:
- Add opt-in quick-lint presubmit lane that reduces setup time for small PRs
- Introduce presubmit-prober to warm runner caches and reduce cold-start latency
- Introduce Oxide dep cleanser for devdep hygiene (dry-run by default)
- Sparse-fetch wrapper for faster installs in quick lanes
notes: Ops: monitor presubmit-latency and oxide false-positive rate. Backstop: quick-lint is opt-in and cannot block merges unless repo config is changed.
